## I need one figure from you

**How many years of backend engineering experience do you have?** The summary has no years, dates, or role durations, so I can't state or calculate the figure, and I won't guess.

### What it costs to leave it out

- **The requirement is a number, and the summary has no number.** "8 years of backend engineering experience" is a threshold. A recruiter checking it will look for a figure, find none, and may assume you fall short.
- **Automated screening may filter you out.** Many applicant tracking systems match years of experience against the posting's minimum.
- **The current content can't fill the gap.** Three areas of work suggest breadth but say nothing about duration. That could mean three years or twelve.
- **You'd lose your strongest match.** If you have 8+ years, stating it up front hits the exact requirement. Leaving it out turns a clear pass into a judgment call.

### Draft ready for the figure

> Backend engineer with **[X] years** of experience building transactional services. Most recently built and operated a settlement pipeline processing 40,000 orders per day. Previous work spans payment reconciliation and inventory systems.

If X is 8 or more, this meets the requirement as written. If it's under 8, tell me and I'll rework the summary to lead with scale and scope rather than tenure.

### If you'd rather not give a figure

> Backend engineer specializing in high-volume transactional systems. Most recently built and operated a settlement pipeline processing 40,000 orders per day, with prior work across payment reconciliation and inventory systems.

This version reads well, but it doesn't address the 8-year requirement, which carries the risks above.
